title: Azure SQL Database: DTU and vCore, serverless and elastic pools

videos.script: Quitanda's orders live in SQL Server, on one machine in a cupboard of the office. Somebody patches it when they remember. A job copies it to a disk next to it every night. {{cupboard}} Azure SQL Database is Microsoft's offer to take that machine away. The hardware, the patches, the backups and the failover become Microsoft's job. What stays yours is everything inside the database. The schema, the slow query, the missing index. {{yours}} You will run the engine underneath it on your laptop, in SQL Server's own container. A support query reads three hundred and thirty-seven pages to find fifteen orders. One index takes it to two. {{index}} Then the bill. Azure sells the same engine two ways. The DTU model sells a bundle, with one number. The vCore model sells the parts, and it is where your old licences count. {{models}} Serverless bills by the second and pauses when nobody connects. A short program finds the hour where it stops being cheaper. {{serverless}} And an elastic pool shares one amount of compute among many databases, which works until they all get busy at once. {{pool}}
